subject: Request: subvendor permission & DPA evidence — Acme Corporation
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acmecorp.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: subvendor permission & DPA evidence — Acme Corporation

Hi Priyom / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our security team reviewed Redwood's hosted offering and we are moving to the procurement step. Two asks from our side before legal signs the Order Form: 

1) We need formal permission to onboard SubCloud (subvendor) as a subprocessor for log aggregation. Their proposed scope is limited to encrypted logs and retention matching our DPA. Please confirm if Redwood can accept SubCloud as a flow-down subprocessor or if we need a formal flowdown amendment.

2) Please provide the DPA evidence bundle (SOC2 summary, encryption-at-rest confirmation, subprocessors list, and data deletion flow) so we can attach it to our vendor review. I attached their proposed MSA redlines and a draft Order Form with the SubCloud callout.

Attachments: subcloud_proposal.pdf (external), redline_MSA_ACME_20270214.pdf (ACME redlines)

We'd prefer to resolve this by end of week and can hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

Cheers,
Emily Zhao
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corporation
(attachment: subcloud_proposal.pdf)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: subvendor permission & DPA evidence — Acme Corporation

Emily — thanks for the clear summary. Appreciate the attachments. Quick reply with next steps from our side: 

- We can provisionally approve SubCloud as a subprocessor for the narrow log-aggregation use case, pending evidence review and a signed flow-down. We typically require either (a) a signed subprocessor flow-down executed by SubCloud, or (b) an Order Form amendment that expressly names SubCloud and incorporates the DPA flow-down.

- I'm attaching a short checklist for evidence we need (SOC2 Type II summary, encryption cert, subproc list, data deletion SLA). If ACME can get the SubCloud evidence bundle to us, we will run a quick internal triage.

Action items:
1) Laura — can you validate whether the redline to Section 6.2 in ACME's MSA (PDF attached) is something we can accept as-is, or whether Legal should propose counter-language?
2) Marissa — please route the SubCloud vendor evidence to Rishi (Legal) and set up a 30-min triage for Tue 2/16.

Emily — if you prefer, we can produce the flow-down template and circulate for signature; otherwise we can accept an Order Form amendment. Either way, we'll need the evidence bundle before we finalize.

Best,
Priyom
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redline_review_checklist.pdf)

Subject: Re: Request: subvendor permission & DPA evidence — Acme Corporation

Priyom / Marissa — looping in Rishi for legal on the redlines. Quick read: ACME's proposed change narrows our liability flow-down in Section 6.2 and adds a request to bind SubCloud directly to the DPA. Two points: 

- From a commercial perspective, naming SubCloud in the Order Form amendment is acceptable. It gives ACME visibility and is a straightforward flow-down.
- From a risk perspective, Rishi — can Legal confirm whether the proposed language (see attached PDF redline) inadvertently expands ACME's ability to dictate retention policies beyond the DPA? If so, we should propose a limited carve (retain the DPA retention schedule and forbid ACME from unilateral retention extensions).

Marissa — if Legal signs off, prioritize getting a flow-down executed. If Rishi wants an alternate redline, I recommend we ask ACME to accept our counter and hold signature until that's resolved. For approvals above threshold, we may need an OK from Sales Leadership (Priyom) and VP of Revenue.

Laura
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround. Per your ask, attached is the SubCloud evidence bundle and a signed MSA addendum that names SubCloud as an allowed subprocessor (signature redacted).

Summary of what we provided: 
- subproc_evidence_bundle.zip (SOC2 summary, encryption cert, subproc list)
- signed_orderform_addendum.pdf (ACME-signed addendum naming SubCloud)

We have a legal rep available Tue 2/16 at 11:00 PT if you want to triage the MSA redlines and confirm flow-down language. Otherwise, we are fine with Redwood providing a flow-down template and SubCloud signing directly.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood confirms acceptance of the signed addendum + evidence or provides revised redline by EOD Tue 2/16.
2) If required, schedule a three-way call with SubCloud to close outstanding items.

Best,
Emily Zhao
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Corporation
